column5: Password and other credentials are sent in the URL query string instead of the request body
column6: login at src/services/auth.ts:69-83 calls api.post with the /login path - a null body - and a params object at :77 so email - password and mobile are serialised into the query string rather than the body. The same pattern repeats at :32 for registerUser where password and password_confirmation are sent to /register - at :22 for verifyUser (/verify-user) and at :201 for forgotPassword (/forget-password). axios places the params object in the URL and sends a null body so the full credential set appears in the request line. Every hop that records request lines keeps them - web server access logs - reverse proxies - CDNs and APM traces. Contrast phoneLogin at :119-138 which correctly sends a body and moves only the bearer token into a header so the correct pattern already exists in the same file.
column10: Any login or registration attempt. Standard web server or proxy access logging which records the request line including the query string.
column11: 1. Open the login sheet and submit any email and password. 2. Inspect the outgoing request in the devtools network tab and read the request URL. 3. Confirm the password appears as a query parameter while the request body is null.
column12: Credentials travel in the POST body only and never appear in the URL.
column13: email - password - mobile and password_confirmation are all query parameters on the request URL.
column14: Plaintext passwords are written into every access log and proxy log along the request path and are readable by anyone with log access. Because users reuse passwords the exposure reaches beyond this application. Log shipping and retention widen it further.
column15: Send these payloads as the request body rather than as params for /login - /register - /verify-user and /forget-password. Confirm the panel accepts body parameters on those routes first and coordinate the change because the API is shared with other production clients.

column5: The bearer token and the full user record are persisted to localStorage by redux-persist
column6: The redux-persist configuration at src/lib/redux/store.ts:12-16 lists auth in the whitelist so the entire auth slice is serialised to localStorage under the persist key root. authSlice at src/lib/redux/slices/authSlice.ts:5-15 holds access_token and the complete user object so both are written on every login through the login reducer at :26-30. This is a SECOND copy of the session and is distinct from issue 3 which covers the JavaScript readable cookie - the fix differs because this one is redux-persist configuration rather than cookie flags. localStorage also has no expiry so this copy outlives the cookie.
column11: 1. Log in. 2. Open the devtools application tab and read the localStorage key persist:root. 3. Find access_token and the user object inside the serialised auth slice.
column12: The session token is not written to localStorage - persist only non sensitive auth fields such as isLoggedIn and rehydrate the session from the cookie or the profile endpoint.
column13: access_token and the full user record including name - email and mobile are stored in localStorage in clear text with no expiry.
column14: A second XSS reachable copy of the bearer token plus user PII. Because localStorage never expires the token survives a browser restart and remains replayable on a shared machine long after the cookie has gone.
column15: Remove auth from the redux-persist whitelist or add a persist transform that strips access_token and the user PII before serialisation - then rehydrate auth state on boot from the session cookie or from /user/profile.

column5: The cart slice is persisted although both CLAUDE files explicitly forbid persisting it
column6: The redux-persist whitelist at src/lib/redux/store.ts:16 contains cart. Root CLAUDE.md section 7.1 lists the allowlist as auth - offlineCart - recentlyViewed and search - and src/lib/redux/CLAUDE.md states plainly that cart must not be persisted because it is a server mirror that is always re-fetched on login. cartSlice is persisted anyway so a stale server cart is rehydrated from localStorage on every boot and rendered before any revalidation completes. Separately search is absent from the whitelist which also contradicts root CLAUDE.md 7.1 - but the inline comment at :16 shows that exclusion is deliberate so only the cart entry is treated as a defect here.
column10: Logged in user with items in the server cart. The cart has since changed elsewhere - another device or an admin action or a price change.
column11: 1. Add items to the cart and allow the state to persist. 2. Change that cart from another device or change a product price server side. 3. Reopen the storefront and read the cart before the refetch resolves.
column12: The cart is not persisted - it is fetched from the server so the first paint shows either server truth or a loading state.
column13: The previous cart is rehydrated from localStorage and rendered including stale quantities and stale prices until the refetch replaces it.
column14: Customer briefly sees outdated cart contents and pricing which is most visible on a slow connection. The documented state ownership and the shipped configuration disagree which will mislead the next person to read either CLAUDE file.
column15: Remove cart from the whitelist so the server mirror is always fetched. If persisting it is a deliberate offline decision then update both CLAUDE files to match and document what guarantees revalidation before the cart is shown.

column5: Firebase auth error messages and setup toasts are hard-coded English and bypass i18n
column6: getFirebaseErrorMessage at src/lib/firebase.ts:247-271 returns twelve hard-coded English strings for the Firebase auth error codes it maps at :251 :253 :255 :257 :259 :261 :263 :265 and :267 - and falls back to the raw Firebase SDK error.message at :269. Those strings reach users through addToast in src/helpers/auth.ts at :265 for apple login - :322 for sign up and :386 for resend OTP - code which uses i18n.t for every other string it renders. src/lib/firebase.ts also raises English toasts directly at :88-90 - :129-131 - :214-217 and :221-224. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar.
column10: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any Firebase auth failure such as an expired code or the too many requests limit.
column11: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Request a phone OTP and enter an incorrect code or trigger the too many attempts limit. 3. Read the toast that appears.
column12: The message renders in the active language from the locale bundles like every other auth message in the same flow.
column13: The message renders in English whatever the selected language - and the default branch can surface a raw Firebase SDK string that was never written for end users.
column14: Hindi and Arabic users meet untranslated English at the exact moment authentication fails which is a high friction point in the funnel. The default branch can also leak raw SDK wording into the UI.
column15: Map each Firebase error code to a translation key and resolve it with t() at the call site - add the keys to en - hi and ar - and give the default branch a generic translated fallback instead of error.message. Then run npm run scan:i18n.
